Kernel two-sample test (MMD)

Source: R/dsg_benchmark.R
dsg_mmd_test.Rd

Permutation test of whether two samples come from the same distribution, using the maximum mean discrepancy (Gretton et al., 2012) with a random-trees kernel: the similarity of two points is the share of totally random trees in which they fall in the same leaf. This is the test used to verify virtual drift in the reference implementation of Hinder et al. (2026).

Usage

dsg_mmd_test(x1, x2, n_perm = 2500, n_trees = 100, max_depth = 5)

Arguments

x1, x2

Data frames or matrices with the same numeric columns.

n_perm

Number of permutations.

n_trees, max_depth

Size of the random-trees embedding.

Value

list with the MMD statistic and the permutation p_value (share of permutations with a larger statistic)

References

Gretton, A., Borgwardt, K. M., Rasch, M. J., Scholkopf, B., and Smola, A. (2012). A kernel two-sample test. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 13, 723-773.

Examples

set.seed(1)
same <- dsg_mmd_test(matrix(stats::rnorm(200), 100), matrix(stats::rnorm(200), 100), n_perm = 200)
shifted <- dsg_mmd_test(matrix(stats::rnorm(200), 100), matrix(stats::rnorm(200, 1), 100),
                        n_perm = 200)
c(same$p_value, shifted$p_value)
#> [1] 0.45 0.00
